The GrowthCred field guide

Stuck choosing an AI workshop or done-for-you automation? You pick the route before you spend.

Buying your wrong option wastes time, cash, or both.

Here is how to match AI training or automation to your actual task. Business decisions stay yours.

Quick answer

You pick a workshop only for one bounded task.

4 min read

You'll learn

  1. When a workshop fits a single task and when implementation fits a multi-step process.
  2. How five practical questions expose ownership, costs, and post-handover duties before you commit.

Why listen to GrowthCred

GrowthCred is a Johannesburg AI implementation and training company. I teach AI at Melsoft Academy. I helped build an isiZulu and English speech AI system. It was presented at Parliament in Cape Town.

1Workshops fail when you want a managed system, not practice time

The problem

  1. Workshops need your time to practise.
  2. Brief, and check output on a real task. If you expect a managed service or have no time to run it. Training stalls.

The way through

  1. You pick a workshop only for one bounded task.
  2. Like drafting a proposal from approved facts. Keep your business info current. You run the workflow yourself after the session.

Training teaches you to run a bounded task. It does not run the business.

2Implementation fails when you buy a demo instead of a working flow

The problem

  1. Tools change, permissions shift, and messy inputs break fragile setups.
  2. A slick demo hides how exceptions behave across connected tools and approvals.

The way through

  1. You choose implementation when data moves across tools.
  2. Several people approve work, or exceptions need testing. Test on your real examples. You agree on handover vs ongoing support upfront.

A delivered project and a managed service are different jobs, so agree on both.

3Five questions separate clear ownership from expensive confusion for you

The problem

  1. Teams rush into buying before deciding who supplies inputs.
  2. Checks work, or owns accounts. Unclear scope leaves buyers guessing what support costs after launch.

The way through

  1. You check time, scope, cost, ownership, and support before choosing training or implementation.
  2. You confirm who controls accounts, documents, and configuration, plus how changes get quoted.

Someone in your business must own the workflow, whatever option you pick.

4One weekly task shows whether to start with a workshop or a scope check for you

The problem

  1. Guessing between training and implementation leads to stalled tools or mismatched expectations.
  2. Repeating a slow manual task every week without clear rules wastes hours.

The way through

  1. You write down one weekly task.
  2. Its inputs, what good output looks like, and current time spent. You use a safe browser test for a workshop. Or request a scope check if integrations and checks are heavy.

You start with one real weekly task. You confirm scope and costs, and keep control.

If you want a workshop to practise one task or a scope check for a connected workflow. GrowthCred keeps your two offers separate. Confirms availability, scope, and every cost upfront. You can decide without pressure.
